IDEA TITLE​

2​

@SIH Idea submission- Template​

Your Team Name​

​

Proposed Solution​

  • •"Gram Swasthya Setu" – offline-first AI health app for ASHA/CHO workers​

  • •Bluetooth vitals kit + on-device AI triage → Green/Yellow/Red, no internet needed​

Detailed Explanation​

  • •ASHA/CHO records vitals; AI gives instant risk level; syncs to ABDM when online​

  • •Yellow → auto-books eSanjeevani; Red → referral + transport; dashboard tracks trends​

How It Addresses the Problem​

  • •Kills "go or not go" confusion with instant on-site triage​

  • •Shifts digital burden to trusted worker; ends referral guesswork​

Innovation & Uniqueness​

  • •Covers the pre-diagnosis gap eSanjeevani/hospitals miss​

  • •True offline AI, worker-run, integrates with ABDM/eSanjeevani (not a duplicate)​

TECHNICAL APPROACH​

3​

@SIH Idea submission- Template​

Your Team Name​

Technologies to be Used​

  • •Frontend: Flutter / React Native (cross-platform, offline-capable mobile app)​

  • •AI/Voice: Python, TensorFlow/TensorFlow Lite (triage model), Google Speech-to-Text / Bhashini (multilingual voice NLP)​

  • •Backend: Node.js (Express) / Django-FastAPI + PostgreSQL / Firebase for records & appointments​

  • •Integrations & hardware: ABDM/ABHA + eSanjeevani APIs; SMS/USSD gateway (e.g. Twilio) for offline ASHA-worker fallback; smartphone-only, no extra hardware needed​

Methodology and Process for Implementation​

  • •Patient describes symptoms by voice/text (multilingual) → AI Symptom Checker​

  • •AI generates Triage Result (severity + recommendation) → nearest hospital Appointment booking (date/time)​

  • •Consultation outcome auto-updates lifelong digital Health Records (ABDM-linked, shareable)​

  • •No internet → app shows nearest ASHA worker's contact for Offline Help​

​

​

FEASIBILITY AND VIABILITY​

4​

@SIH Idea submission- Template​

Your Team Name​

Feasibility Analysis​

  • •Builds on existing ASHA/CHO workforce and Ayushman Bharat HWCs – no new manpower needed​

  • •Runs on smartphones only – no extra hardware; integrates with existing ABDM/eSanjeevani infrastructure​

  • •Can pilot in a single district under NHM before state/national scale-up​

Potential Challenges and Risks​

  • •Low digital literacy and limited smartphone/data access among some rural users​

  • •Intermittent internet connectivity for teleconsults and data sync​

  • •Data privacy/consent concerns; government approval and procurement timelines​

Strategies for Overcoming Challenges​

  • •Voice-first, icon-driven UI in local languages (Bhashini) to bypass literacy barriers​

  • •Offline-first design with SMS/ASHA-worker fallback for zero-connectivity areas​

  • •ABHA-linked consent framework and encryption; phased rollout via NHM partnership for smoother approvals​

​

​

IMPACT AND BENEFITS​

5​

@SIH Idea submission- Template​

Your Team Name​

Potential Impact on the Target Audience​

  • •Directly serves rural patients, pregnant women, children, elderly & chronic-disease patients facing long travel for basic care​

  • •Empowers ASHA/CHO workers with an AI decision-support tool, easing their workload​

  • •Scales to India's ~65% rural population, where specialist shortfall at CHCs runs as high as ~80%​

Benefits of the Solution​

  • •Social: reduces unnecessary travel and wait times; builds trust via multilingual, voice-first access​

  • •Economic: cuts patient transport/opportunity-cost losses; reduces overcrowding at CHCs by filtering non-urgent cases​

  • •Health: faster emergency detection and referral improves survival odds; lifelong digital health records improve continuity of care​

  • •Environmental: fewer long-distance trips to hospitals for cases that didn't need to travel​

​

​

RESEARCH AND REFERENCES​

6​

@SIH Idea submission- Template​

Your Team Name​

Research Findings​

  • •eSanjeevani: 43+ crore teleconsultations (PIB, Nov 2025)​

  • •79.5% specialist shortfall at rural CHCs (Rural Health Stats 2021-22)​

  • •India: ~0.7 doctors/1,000 population (WHO 2022)​

  • •Worker-assisted telehealth models cut access barriers (Sood et al., 2025)​

  • •Rural teleconsult awareness only ~2.2% (Parameshwarappa & Olickal, 2023)​
